lines.text: Do you know the fastest thing humans have ever built is flying through the Sun's atmosphere?
This is NASA's Parker Solar Probe, built from NASA's own 3D model. It was the first NASA spacecraft named after a living person, Eugene Parker.
On December twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-four, it passed six point one million kilometres from the Sun's surface.
It was moving at about six hundred and ninety thousand kilometres an hour. New York to Tokyo, in under a minute.
Its heat shield is built to take about one thousand four hundred degrees Celsius.
It's a sandwich. Two thin carbon skins around a foam core eleven centimetres thick. And that foam is ninety-seven percent air.
Right behind it, the spacecraft stays at about thirty degrees. Like a summer day.
Near the Sun, nobody on Earth can steer it. It keeps its shield pointed at the Sun all by itself.
So after the closest pass, the team could only wait. On December twenty-sixth, a beacon came home. Parker was healthy.
Waiting to know if it arrived is the worst part. With Orbi Transfer, you see it live.
A green dot for every person who has your file open right now. And every download, counted the moment it happens.
